canopy.layout.markdownDescription: Folder layout and hidden repositories. Edited from the CANOPY view; saved in the workspace.

canopy.profiles.markdownDescription: Saved clone/switch profiles. Edited from the Profiles panel.

canopy.repositories.markdownDescription: Extra repository paths to track besides the ones found by scanning.

canopy.scanRoots.markdownDescription: Extra folders to scan for Git repositories (workspace folders are always scanned). Supports `~` and `${workspaceFolder}`.

canopy.scanDepth.markdownDescription: How many folder levels below each scan root to look for repositories (0–10). Use `-1` for no limit; scanning still stops after 50,000 folders, skips `canopy.scanExclude` folders, and does not look inside repositories unless `canopy.scanNested` is on.

canopy.scanNested.markdownDescription: Also scan inside repositories for other nested repositories (vendored repos). Submodules declared in `.gitmodules` are found without this and appear under their parent when you expand it.

canopy.autoFetch.intervalMinutes.markdownDescription: Fetch all visible repositories in the background every N minutes. `0` (the default, as with VS Code's `git.autofetch`) turns automatic fetching off; use **Fetch All** when you want updates. Background fetches run two at a time at low priority and never show a sign-in window.

canopy.autoFetch.onFocus.markdownDescription: When automatic fetching is on, also fetch when the window regains focus and the last fetch is older than the interval.

canopy.fetchAllConcurrency.markdownDescription: How many repositories **Fetch All** fetches at once. `0` fetches every repository at once. Dropped connections (e.g. *Connection closed by remote host* when an SSH server limits simultaneous logins) are retried automatically, and each host is signed in to once before the rest of its repositories are fetched.

canopy.fetchPrune.markdownDescription: Prune deleted remote branches on every fetch.

canopy.refreshIntervalSeconds.markdownDescription: Re-read local status of every repository every N seconds (minimum 10) as a fallback to file watching. `0` (the default) turns polling off: saves and changes in `.git` still update status, and **Refresh** re-reads everything on demand.

canopy.useBuiltinGit.markdownDescription: Experimental. For repositories VS Code's own Git already has open, use its status instead of running `git status` a second time. Off by default: measured with 90 repositories, it saved only CANOPY's small share of git processes, and VS Code's Git sometimes reported a saved file late. CANOPY never asks VS Code's Git to open more repositories.

canopy.maxConcurrentGit.markdownDescription: Maximum number of status-reading Git processes CANOPY runs at once. Fetches have their own limit (`canopy.fetchAllConcurrency`), and your own commands never wait.

canopy.gitPath.markdownDescription: Path to the Git executable. Empty uses `git.path`, then `git` on PATH.

canopy.discard.safetyStash.markdownDescription: Save a stash before discarding changes so a discard can be undone.

enumDescriptions: Open the first diff beside the details panel, then keep using that editor group while it is open.
Always open diffs in the second editor column.
canopy.diff.placement.markdownDescription: Where file diffs from the details panel open. Each diff opens as a preview tab, so the next one replaces it.

canopy.stats.maxCommits.markdownDescription: Most recent commits read for the Stats tab of the details panel. Larger values cover more history but take longer on big repositories.

canopy.stats.exclude.markdownDescription: Files left out of line counts in the Stats tab (lockfiles, minified and generated output). A pattern without `/` matches the file name anywhere (`*.min.js`); one with `/` matches from the repository root (`dist/**`).

canopy.graph.maxCommits.markdownDescription: Commits loaded into the commit graph.

canopy.bulkPullMode.markdownDescription: How Pull works when run on several repositories or a folder at once.

canopy.openDetailsOnClick.markdownDescription: Open the details panel when a repository is clicked in the view.

canopy.gitlab.instances.markdownDescription: GitLab servers CANOPY talks to (gitlab.com or self-hosted). Added automatically by **CANOPY: Connect GitLab…**. Access tokens are kept in secret storage, not here.

sshHosts.description: Other host names used in SSH remotes for this server.

canopy.gitlab.refreshMinutes.markdownDescription: Refresh pipeline and merge request status of visible repositories every N minutes. `0` (the default) turns timed refreshing off: status is re-read after **Fetch**, **Refresh**, a push and a branch switch.

canopy.gitlab.cloneProtocol.markdownDescription: Which URL to use when cloning from a GitLab group.

canopy.gitlab.promptToConnect.markdownDescription: Offer to connect when repositories use a GitLab server that is not connected yet.

canopy.github.enabled.markdownDescription: Show GitHub checks and pull requests for repositories on github.com (and on the GitHub Enterprise server in `github-enterprise.uri`).

canopy.github.refreshMinutes.markdownDescription: Refresh GitHub checks and pull request status of visible repositories every N minutes. `0` (the default) turns timed refreshing off: status is re-read after **Fetch**, **Refresh**, a push and a branch switch.

canopy.github.cloneProtocol.markdownDescription: Which URL to use when cloning from a GitHub organization.

canopy.github.promptToConnect.markdownDescription: Offer to sign in when repositories are on GitHub and CANOPY is not signed in yet.

canopy.branchColors.specialNames.markdownDescription: Branch names shown in the **special** color on the Profiles page, for example `main` or `master`.

canopy.branchColors.special.markdownDescription: Color for the special branch names (`canopy.branchColors.specialNames`) on the Profiles page.

canopy.branchColors.other.markdownDescription: Color for all other branch names on the Profiles page.

canopy.branchColors.local.markdownDescription: Color for local branches in the Branch menu of the repository details.

canopy.branchColors.remote.markdownDescription: Color for remote branches in the Branch menu of the repository details.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with CANOPY
walkthroughs.description: Organize your repositories, connect GitLab and share profiles.

steps.title: Find your repositories
steps.description:
CANOPY lists every Git repository in your workspace folders. Add others by hand or point it at folders to scan.
[Add Repository](command:canopy.addRepository)
[Choose Folders to Scan](command:workbench.action.openSettings?%5B%22canopy.scanRoots%22%5D)

steps.title: Connect GitLab or GitHub
steps.description:
See pipelines or checks and merge or pull requests for each repository, and create them without leaving VS Code. Works with gitlab.com, self-hosted GitLab, github.com and GitHub Enterprise.
[Connect GitLab](command:canopy.gitlab.connect)
[Sign in to GitHub](command:canopy.github.connect)

steps.title: Organize into folders
steps.description:
Folders in CANOPY don't depend on where repositories live on disk. Use Edit Layout to drag repos into folders and hide the ones you don't need.
[Edit Layout](command:canopy.editLayout)

steps.title: Clone a GitLab group or GitHub organization
steps.description:
Pick a group or organization, tick the projects you want, and CANOPY clones them into matching folders.
[Clone from GitLab Group](command:canopy.gitlab.cloneFromGroup)
[Clone from GitHub Organization](command:canopy.github.cloneFromGroup)

steps.title: Save and share profiles
steps.description:
A profile records which repositories and branches belong together. Switch to it in one step, or send it to a teammate.
[Open Profiles](command:canopy.openProfiles)
